newsitem.title: USA: NYC Muni Assistance Corp okays $1.4 bln of bonds.
newsitem.headline: NYC Muni Assistance Corp okays $1.4 bln of bonds.

text.p: The board of Municipal Assistance Corp (MAC) of New York City Thursday approved a $1.4 billion refunding bond sale program that starts February 26, the board's chairman said.
There were no opposing votes for the bond sales, which are part of a $2.9 billion financing program, said Edward Regan, chairman of MAC.
New York City's budget will receive some relief from these refunding bond sales.
"There we go," said Regan at the board meeting here. "The $2.9 billion program, with savings for the city's taxpayers, is launched."
The financing plan that would provide New York City with about $250 million over the next 17 months.
The first sale of fixed-rate bonds, set for Feb 26, would total about $494.7 million. The underwriters would be led by Morgan Stanley & Co.

A second sale of $492.4 million of fixed-rate bonds in April would be led by JP Morgan Securities. Smith Barney would lead the syndicate for a third offering of $405 million of variable rate bonds, scheduled for April or May. Goldman Sachs & Co will run the books for a $390.9 million sale of fixed-rate bonds planned for October, MAC said.
In April 1998, MAC would sell $230 million of fixed-rate bonds under the plan. In April 1999, it expected to offer $200 million of fixed-rate bonds.
The $2.9 billion financing program was started in December 1996 with a $667 million refunding sale. MAC was set up in the mid-1970s to rescue the city from a fiscal crisis.
